subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Disc Cams: Shaping Motion with Profiles
description: A fast breakdown of Disc Cams: Shaping Motion with Profiles for builders.

hook.text: Cut an odd shape from a disc, spin it, and the follower dances.

buildup.text: As the cam rotates, its profile pushes a follower up, down, or to the side.

discovery.text: The shape of the cam edge directly encodes the output motion sequence.

twist.text: One cam can produce motions no linkage could match — any curve is possible.

climax.text: Engine valves, sewing machines, and locks all use disc cam profiles.

punchline.text: Carve the right profile and the motion programs itself.

quiz.question: How does a disc cam control motion?
options: Gears inside the cam change the speed of the follower
The cam's edge profile pushes the follower in a programmed path
Springs inside the cam store and release energy to the follower
